RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 20

It depends on your employer's recruitment policies and whether you uncover evidence of procedural unfairness. Many public broadcasters mandate gender-balanced selection panels; if having an all-female panel breached internal hiring policy, that procedural irregularity may be raised through HR or a union.

However, panel composition alone does not prove sex discrimination. In modern broadcasting, digital media expertise is often prioritized over traditional seniority, providing a legitimate basis for the appointment. Alleging gender bias without concrete evidence risks damaging your professional standing as deputy editor.

First, follow up politely on your written feedback. Review how the panel scored candidates against the objective job criteria before deciding whether any challenge is warranted.
